facts.fact: Land Affairs Minister O'Neige N'Sele said on 2026-10-08 that implementation of the December 2025 land law has begun, aiming at digitising the cadastre, with Maluku, N'Sele and Mont-Ngafula in the first phase of digitising Kinshasa's nine land districts.

APA reported on 2026-08-11 that the Ministry of Land Affairs launched training for 250 officials, including 50 Land Title Registrars, with INACO, followed by scanning and indexing of archives in seven pilot land districts as the opening phase of the national Land Registry's digital transformation.

The Ministry of Land Affairs said on 2026-06-12 that a dematerialisation pilot is under way with a digitisation unit making progressive digital archiving operational in seven pilot Kinshasa land districts, with full cadastre digitisation and electronic title security among priorities.

facts.fact: On 5 August 2026 the Ministry of Land Affairs signed a protocol with INaCo to start digitising land administration, with 200 agents trained and land archives sorted and coded in pilot circumscriptions before integration into a digital archiving system.

facts.fact: The land ministry says modular digital solutions have been deployed with ONU-Habitat and CAFI support while full digitisation of the sector is awaited, and the minister told the National Assembly digitisation of titles is strategic.
Fonaredd reports a feasibility study of a land atlas documented 151 land administrations across 26 provinces, and the proposed e-SIF 2.0 would digitise land archives and build a GIS digital cadastre.
A UN-Habitat study validated with the Ministry of Land Affairs found the land digitisation process is still embryonic, with under 15% of plots holding a legal document.

note: Digitisation of land titles is a provision of a bill just passed by the Senate, not a system under way.

facts.fact: The land minister told the Council of Ministers that archive digitisation, begun 17 August 2026 in 17 Kinshasa land districts and extended to Haut-Katanga and Lualaba, had identified 1,822,051 land files, 14.8% digitised, with 561 staff trained and a target of all 149 districts.
